name: Emily Lange
description: Emily Lange is a product designer in Brooklyn, New York, working at the intersection of education and design.
headline: Hi! I’m a product designer based in Brooklyn, New York.
intro: Exploring opportunities to create meaningful impact. I am passionate about using my background in industrial design and education to drive user needs and business goals. My work includes user research, interaction design, prototyping, accessibility and design systems.
intro_aside:
At the moment I’m taking on freelance projects and heading the publication over at [UX of EdTech](https://www.uxedtech.com/).

Previously led design efforts for EdTech startups such as [Clicked](https://www.clicked.com/), [Mucktracker](https://www.mucktracker.com/), and Mindful Digits.
about:
**Glad you’re here!** I’m a product designer based in Brooklyn, New York, passionate about education and design. My background in teaching and human-centered design informs my approach, creating intuitive, mission-driven products that empower and engage.

With 9 years of experience in UX/UI, content strategy, and product design, I’ve worked across industries, from EdTech and digital learning to retail and architecture. I thrive in collaborative environments, and love working with those who are driven by purpose and innovation.

When I’m not designing, you’ll find me exploring restaurants in my neighborhood ([one country at a time in alphabetical order](https://www.instagram.com/localfoods.nyc/)), hosting educational wine tastings, or practicing the art of sashiko.

Let me help you turn your complex idea into a clear, impactful solution. [I wanna hear all about it.](#contact)
clients: European Space Agency, Salesforce, Terra Mater Studios, Impact.ai, Keeping Current Matters, Clicked, Mucktracker, UX of EdTech, Tech Fleet
contact_intro: Have a project in mind, or just want to say hi? Holler below :)
audit_text: Share your website, app or digital product with me and I’ll be happy to take a look at it. I’ll get back to you with a brief audit of what’s working, where visitors might get stuck, and the top changes I’d make first.
